1.translation: At the end of the previous chapter it was said that the one who worships Me with the inner being absorbed in Me is the most united. Śrīdhara now explains what form of the Lord is to be worshiped: “O Pārtha, with the mind attached to Me, the Supreme Lord, taking refuge in Me alone, and practicing yoga, listen to how you will know Me completely, without doubt, together with My manifestations, powers, and lordly glory.”
word_for_word: at the end of the previous chapter
with the inner being gone to Me
devotion to Me is to be practiced
whose mind is attached to Me
together with manifestations, powers, lordly glory, and the like

2.translation: The Lord praises what is about to be taught: “I will explain this knowledge concerning Me together with realization, completely and without remainder.” Here knowledge is scriptural knowledge and realization is direct experience. Having known this, a person proceeding on the path of the highest good has nothing else left to know; through this alone the purpose of life is fulfilled.
word_for_word: for one proceeding here on the path of the highest good

3.translation: Without devotion to Me, knowledge of Me is difficult to attain. Among the countless living beings, those other than human beings do not even turn toward the highest good. Among thousands of human beings, only someone, through the force of exceptionally great merit, strives for perfection—for knowledge of the Self. Even among thousands who strive, only one, through such merit, knows the Self; and among thousands who have perfected knowledge of the Self, only one knows Me, the Supreme Self, through My grace and in truth. Thus knowledge of Me, though it is to be taught to you, is exceedingly rare.
word_for_word: of those other than human beings
through the force of exceptionally great merit

4.translation: Śrīdhara now explains the Lord’s nature as the agent of creation and the rest through prakṛti, distinguishing a lower and a higher nature. “Earth, water, fire, air, space, mind, intellect, and ego—this is My eightfold divided prakṛti.” One reading takes the first five as the subtle elements with their qualities, mind as the ego that causes them, intellect as mahat, and ego as the ignorance that causes it. Another takes the first five as the gross elements together with their subtle counterparts, ego as itself and its products including the senses, intellect as mahat, and mind as the unmanifest primordial nature. Though the principles are analyzed in twenty-four ways, they are grouped here into eight divisions.

5.translation: Śrīdhara concludes the description of this lower nature and states the higher nature: “Know this nature of Mine, which is higher and different from this eightfold nature, to be the living principle.” It is higher because, in the form of conscious awareness and the knower of the field, it sustains this world through its own actions.
word_for_word: because it exists for another’s sake
having the nature of the living being
in the form of the living principle
in the form of the knower of the field

6.translation: Śrīdhara shows that both natures are the causes of the Lord’s creation and the rest: know that all beings, from the immovable to the moving, have these two natures as their causes. The insentient nature transforms into bodies; the conscious nature, an aspect of Me, enters bodies as the enjoyer and sustains them through its own actions. These two natures arise from Me. Therefore I alone am the source—the supreme cause—from which the entire world together with its prakṛti arises, and I alone am its dissolution, into which it is withdrawn.
word_for_word: consisting of the immovable and moving
transforms in the form of bodies
of the entire world together with its prakṛti

7.translation: Because the Lord is the source of both natures, there is nothing higher than Him—nothing that is an independent cause superior to Him for the creation and dissolution of the world. He is also the cause of its continuance: “All this world is strung on Me, as jewels on a thread,” meaning that it is woven into and dependent upon Me.

8.translation: The Lord elaborates His role as the support of the world through five expressions: “I am the taste in water, O Kaunteya; I am the light in the moon and sun; I am the syllable Oṃ in all the Vedas, sound in space, and human exertion in people.” In each case Śrīdhara understands the Lord as present through the corresponding excellence or subtle principle.
word_for_word: I am the taste in water
through the manifestation in the form of the subtle principle of taste
the light of the moon and sun
in the form of the subtle principle of sound

9.translation: “I am pure fragrance in the earth, and I am the light in fire; I am life in all beings and austerity in ascetics.” Śrīdhara explains pure fragrance as the unmodified scent, or, as a divine manifestation, the excellence of fragrant scent; the Lord is the subtle principle of fragrance supported by earth. He is the fire’s natural brilliance, the life that sustains breath and lifespan in all beings, and the austerity of ascetics such as forest-dwellers, expressed as endurance of the pairs of opposites.
word_for_word: in the form of endurance of the pairs

10.translation: “Know Me, O Pārtha, as the eternal seed of all beings, moving and unmoving.” Śrīdhara explains this seed as the power to produce effects of the same kind, eternal because it is woven through all successive effects; it is the Lord’s manifestation, not an individual seed that perishes. “I am the intelligence of the intelligent and the splendor of the splendid”—their discernment and excellence.
word_for_word: of all moving and unmoving beings
the capacity to produce an effect of the same kind
not something that perishes in each individual

11.translation: “I am the strength of the strong, free from desire and attachment; I am desire in beings that is not opposed to dharma, O best of the Bharatas.” Śrīdhara distinguishes desire for an unattained object, which is rajasic, from attachment or thirst for an attained or greater object, which is tamasic; the Lord is the strength free from both. He is the sattvic capacity to perform one’s own dharma, and the desire in one’s spouse that serves only the lawful purpose of producing children.
word_for_word: even when a desired object has been obtained
directed toward a greater object and coloring the mind
the sattvic capacity to perform one’s own dharma
desire not opposed to one’s own dharma

12.translation: “Know that whatever other states are sattvic, rajasic, or tamasic arise from Me alone.” Sattvic states include tranquility and restraint; rajasic states include hatred and pride; tamasic states include sorrow and delusion. They arise in beings according to their own actions, as effects of the three qualities of My prakṛti. Yet I am not in them, meaning I am not dependent on them as a living being is; they, however, exist under My control.
word_for_word: in beings according to their own actions
because they are effects of the three qualities of My nature
but I am not in them
I am not dependent on them
they exist in Me / under Me

13.translation: Why does the world not know the Lord of this kind? Śrīdhara answers: this entire world is deluded by the three kinds of guṇa-made states described earlier, such as desire and greed. Therefore it does not know Me, who am beyond these states, untouched by them, their controller, and therefore imperishable and changeless.
word_for_word: by the three kinds of states made of the guṇas
the modifications of the guṇas described earlier
by desire, greed, and the like

14.translation: The Lord’s power, called māyā, is divine, beyond the ordinary, and exceedingly wondrous; it consists of the modifications of the guṇas such as sattva and is difficult to cross. Yet those who take refuge in Me alone and worship Me with undivided devotion cross this māyā, difficult though it is, and thereby come to know Me.
word_for_word: consisting of modifications of guṇas beginning with sattva

15.translation: Why, then, do not all worship the Lord alone? The lowest among people do not take refuge in Me: they are deluded and devoid of discrimination, and this is because they are sinful in character. Their knowledge, even if produced through the instruction of scripture and teacher, has been taken away by māyā. Having adopted a demonic disposition—such as hypocrisy, pride, conceit, anger, and harshness described later—they do not worship Me.
word_for_word: do not take refuge in Me
hypocrisy, pride, conceit, anger, and harshness
whose knowledge has been taken away by māyā
born from instruction of scripture and teacher

16.translation: Those who have performed merit in previous births worship Me; according to the gradation of that merit they are four kinds, O Arjuna: the afflicted, overcome by illness and the like; the seeker of knowledge, who desires knowledge of the Self; the seeker of wealth, who longs for an object that will provide enjoyment here or hereafter; and the knower, who knows the Self. An afflicted person with prior merit worships Me; otherwise he continues in saṃsāra by worshiping lesser deities.
word_for_word: whose merit was performed in previous births
overcome by illness and the like
one who desires knowledge of the Self
the seeker of wealth / desired objects
one who longs for an object that is a means of enjoyment
according to the gradation of merit

17.translation: Among these, the knower is distinguished: he is constantly united with Me and has one-pointed devotion, devotion to Me alone. Because the knower has no identification with the body and the rest, mental distraction is absent; therefore constant union and exclusive devotion are possible for him, not for the others. For this reason I am exceedingly dear to him, and he is dear to Me.
word_for_word: because of absence of identification with the body and the rest
because of absence of mental distraction
I am dear to the knower
and he is dear to Me

18.translation: Are the other three devotees therefore not dear to the Lord? No: all these are noble and great, and all are destined for liberation. Yet the knower is My very Self, this is My settled view. For he is inwardly united, his mind fixed on Me alone, and he has taken refuge in Me as the unsurpassed, highest destination; he regards no result apart from Me.
word_for_word: but the knower is the Self itself
whose mind is fixed on Me alone
has taken refuge in Me alone

19.translation: After many births, through the gradual accumulation of merit, in the final birth the person of knowledge takes refuge in Me, seeing with the vision of the Self of all: “Vāsudeva is everything—moving and unmoving.” Such a great soul, whose vision is not limited, is exceedingly rare.
word_for_word: at the end of many births
through a gradual accumulation of merit
with the vision of the Self of all

20.translation: It has already been said that even those with desires worship Me, the Supreme Lord, for the sake of obtaining those desires and are gradually released. But those who are intensely rajasic or tamasic and overwhelmed by desire worship lesser deities and continue in saṃsāra. Their desires—for a son, fame, victory over an enemy, and the like—steal their discrimination; they worship lesser deities such as spirits, ghosts, and yakṣas. Adopting the observance prescribed for worshiping each deity, such as fasting, they worship a particular deity while constrained by their own nature, shaped by previous practice and latent impressions.
word_for_word: concerning a son, fame, victory over an enemy, and the like
deities such as spirits, ghosts, and yakṣas
characterized by fasting and the like
through latent impressions of previous practice

21.translation: Among them, whichever devotee wishes to worship whichever deity-form with faith—each deity-form is in fact My own form—I, the indwelling Lord, establish that very faith of that devotee, directed toward that form, as firm and unwavering.
word_for_word: in the form of a deity

22.translation: That devotee, endowed with firm faith, undertakes the worship of that deity-form and receives from it the desires he has formed. Yet Śrīdhara makes clear that those results are established and produced by Me, the indwelling Lord; the particular deities are dependent on Me and are My forms.
word_for_word: by Me as the indwelling Lord of each deity
because the deities are dependent on Me

23.translation: Although all deities are forms of Me and their worship is therefore, in reality, worship of Me, and although I alone give the respective results, there is nevertheless a difference in the results obtained by those who worship deities and by those who worship Me directly. For people of limited understanding and restricted vision, even the fruit I grant is finite and perishable. Worshipers of the gods go to the gods, whereas My devotees reach Me, the beginningless and endless supreme bliss.
word_for_word: I alone am the giver of each result

24.translation: Why, then, do not all people abandon the other deities and worship the Lord alone, when the effort is similar and the result is greater? People of small understanding think that I, who am unmanifest and beyond the manifest world, have become manifest in human, fish, tortoise, and other forms. They do not know My supreme nature, which is imperishable and unsurpassed. They see the Lord’s pure and exalted sattvic forms, manifested playfully to protect the world, as material bodies produced by their own karma and no different from other deities; therefore they fail to honor Me and choose the other deities for their quick results, which are finite.
word_for_word: when there is a great difference in result
in human, fish, tortoise, and other forms
a form of pure and exalted sattva
a material body produced by its own karma

25.translation: The Lord is not manifest to the whole world; He is manifest to His devotees alone, because He is covered by yoga-māyā. Śrīdhara explains yoga as the Lord’s own inconceivable arrangement, the wondrous power by which the impossible is made possible. Covered by it, the deluded world does not recognize Me as unborn and imperishable.
word_for_word: I am not manifest to everyone
skill in making the impossible possible
deluded regarding knowledge of My nature

26.translation: The Lord now shows His supreme nature through His unobscured power of knowledge: “I know all beings that have passed away, that are present, and that will be, O Arjuna—all moving and unmoving beings across the three times. But no one knows Me.” Śrīdhara explains that the Lord can rest upon māyā without being deluded by it, whereas māyā deludes others; this is well known in the world.
word_for_word: because of being the support of māyā
absence of delusion of its own support
because of being deluded by My māyā

27.translation: Śrīdhara explains why this ignorance becomes firm. When the gross body has arisen at creation, desire arises toward what is agreeable to it and aversion toward what is disagreeable. From these arises delusion concerning the pairs—heat and cold, pleasure and pain, and the like—which is the loss of discrimination. Through it all beings enter deep delusion and a strong identification: “I am happy; I am suffering.” Therefore they do not know Me.
word_for_word: the cause of the firmness of ignorance
desire toward what is agreeable to it
aversion toward what is disagreeable to it
heat, cold, pleasure, pain, and the like

28.translation: Why, then, are some people seen worshiping the Lord? Those who have practiced merit and whose accumulated sin—the entire obstacle—has come to an end are released from delusion born of the pairs of opposites. With firm vows and one-pointed devotion, they worship Me.
word_for_word: of those accustomed to practicing merit
freed from delusion caused by the pairs

29.translation: Those who strive, taking refuge in Me for freedom from old age and death, know that supreme Brahman, know the entire adhyātma—the pure Self distinct from the body and the rest—and know all karma, including the means to attain it and its hidden meaning.
word_for_word: for freedom from old age and death
distinct from the body and the rest
the means by which That is to be attained

30.translation: Śrīdhara removes the fear that such a devotee might fall away from yoga: the Lord will explain the meanings of adhibhūta and the other terms in the following chapter. Those who know Me together with adhibhūta, adhidaiva, and adhiyajña, with minds joined and attached to Me, know Me even at the time of departure, at death; they do not become bewildered then and forget Me. Therefore there is no fear of a fall from yoga for My devotees.
word_for_word: the principle concerning beings / material elements
whose minds are attached to Me
even at the time of death
